thread:
incident-bot: [P1] serving-runtime pod rtm-55 crashed repeatedly -> GPU OOM detected in decode path. Instance: gke-prod-us-west1-a-rtm-55. Auto-retry triggered.

maya: paging oncall-ml (I'm paged). seeing a flurry of OOMs + container restarts across 3 nodes. marking impact: streaming endpoints returning 502 / dropped frames.

chris: on it. seeing repeated log line: `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.25 GiB` then `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'`. attaching log excerpt.

chris: ```
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] E rtm: kernel.cu:234 CUDA error: out of memory 
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] E rtm: decode.cc:1123 failed to allocate kv cache segment (size=3.25GiB)
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] W rtm: session: token_stream runaway detection tripped: len_out>100000
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] F rtm: process crashed (SIGABRT)
```

devon: that `len_out>100000` looks like a runaway generation. did we push any model variants or prompt-template changes in the last hour?

maya: support-bot shows a deploy 175123 to `gptx-decoder-v2` 08:58 UTC. rolling back that deploy is likely high-risk for traffic. we should apply mitigations first.

sam: +1 on mitigations. triage plan: 1) reduce streaming concurrency / global throttle 2) enforce per-request token cap via feature flag 3) failfast requests hitting runaway detection 4) move traffic for heavy customers to fallback model 5) cordon tainted nodes for inspection.

anna: supporting customer comms. affected customers: CUST-873 (streaming chat), CUST-421 (batch embeddings) showed increased errors. I'm preparing a short note.

opsbot: executed: `kubectl cordon gke-prod-us-west1-a-rtm-55` (node cordoned).

chris: applied temporary runtime flag: `max_output_tokens=2048` -> this caps big runs. also enabled `runaway_protect=true` which stops streams that exceed token threshold and returns 429.

maya: command to toggle flag: ```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"flag":"max_output_tokens","value":2048}'
```

devon: also reduced per-pod concurrency: patched HPA and set `RTM_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4` for the heavy deployment to reduce OOM frequency while we investigate memory leak.

support-bot: notif -> CUST-873: "We see intermittent streaming drops; we've applied a temporary token cap and routing changes. We'll follow up with details."

chris: quick note on root cause hypothesis: new decoder change (v2) altered streaming termination logic; in some prompts `max_tokens` was ignored and the decoder loop appended tokens until memory exhaustion. not seeing evidence of model size change.

sam: agree. next steps: 1) isolate a reproducer with representative prompt, 2) rollback decoder change in canary if reproducer confirmed, 3) cordon/inspect one crashed node for GPU memory leaks, 4) prepare permanent guardrails (default client caps).

maya: devon, can you run a controlled reproduce against canary? use `--max_new_tokens unset` to mimic bad clients.

devon: running now against canary (rtm-canary-3). reproducer ran and hit runaway detection after ~60s. captured minimal repro prompt and added to incident artifact (link: https://artifacts.internal/iss/1756789012).

chris: reproduction log shows decoder enters long loop when returned ``stop_token`` isn't emitted; patch idea: add a hard safety counter in decode loop (`if tokens_generated > FLAGS.max_output_tokens then abort`) — will open PR for v2.

maya: open PR and also prepare rollback patch. PR #3245 created by chris with safety counter.

chris: rolling canary rollback to v1 on canary first to validate impact. `deployctl rollback rtm canary --to v1` started.

incident-bot: Deploy rollback triggered by chris at 2026-03-15T09:52:10Z.

opsbot: drain command: `kubectl drain gke-prod-us-west1-a-rtm-55 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` started as part of node inspection.

anna: Sent updated comms to customers: "We've identified the source as a decoder change that could ignore client-set token limits in rare prompts. We've applied a temporary cap and are rolling back the canary. We'll provide a follow-up within 2 hours."

maya: handoff: i'm going offline in 20m. chris will be primary oncall for next two hours. @chris take it away.

chris: oncall ack. continuing: monitoring OOMs, verifying rollback reduces crash rate. setting alerts to 3x baseline for node restarts.

support-bot: ticket created: RINF-INC-2026-1756789012. linked customers: CUST-873, CUST-421.

devon: after rollback, canary is stable. observed 0 OOMs in canary for 15m. promoting rollback to prod in staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

chris: staging rollback at 10% -> no OOMs. moving to 50%.

incident-bot: routing change: 25% of streaming traffic for premium tier rerouted to fallback model `gptx-compact-8q` to relieve pressure.

maya: quick mitigation checklist for postmortem: - ensure default per-request caps (server side), - add unit/integration tests for stop token behavior, - add metrics for token generation per-request, - implement safer decoder loop bounds.

sam: assign owners: chris -> runtime patch + tests, devon -> reproduction harness + perf test, ops (maya) -> node forensics and check for GPU driver issues, anna -> customer follow-ups.

chris: last status update: staged rollback finished 100% at 2026-03-15T10:20:05Z. crash rate back to baseline. will keep monitoring for 2 hours then move to postmortem write-up.

anna: final customer update sent. said they'll keep open support ticket. no SLA credits expected but we're tracking.

maya: thanks team. leaving follow-up items in RINF-INC-2026-1756789012. handing to chris for the postmortem. :white_check_mark:

chris: acknowledged. starting postmortem draft now. will include timeline, root cause (decoder v2 failed to enforce max tokens in specific streaming path), impact (dropped streaming requests for small subset of customers), mitigations (token cap, rollback, node cordon), and action items.
